newsitem.title: USA: Tycoons, students mourn slain son of NY media mogul.
newsitem.headline: Tycoons, students mourn slain son of NY media mogul.

text.p: U.S. media tycoons mourned alongside weeping inner-city high school students on Wednesday at an emotional funeral for the murdered son of Time Warner Inc's top executive.
More than 1,000 mourners packed the funeral service for Jonathan Levin, the son of Time Warner chairman and chief executive Gerald Levin who was an English teacher at a New York City high school.
Levin, 31, was found shot through the head and stabbed on Monday in his one-bedroom Manhattan apartment. He had been bound and gagged, and there was no sign of a forced entry.
A police spokeswoman said no arrests had been made.
In an emotional outpouring, colleagues, friends and relatives praised Levin as a beloved teacher and an inspiration for his students at Taft High School in the gritty South Bronx section of New York.
"In the past 24 hours I've searched and searched for what is to be learned" from Levin's death, Bryant McBride, a longtime friend, said in a breaking voice.

"Cherish your friends, help those who need it, be passionate about what you do and teach kids," he said, sparking a wave of sobs from dozens of students and teachers attending the services at the Park Avenue Synagogue.
Levin's older brother, Lee, said, "I told my brother I loved him and thankfully I did it recently. But I do wish I'd told him that more."
Levin's father, one of the United States' most influential corporate heads, did not speak.
Levin's polished mahogany casket rested at the front of the ornate synagogue, a New York Yankees baseball cap on its top.

The services caused a traffic jam on New York's tony Upper East Side as limousines and onlookers clogged streets. Ear-ringed youths in baggy blue jeans and baseball caps worn backwards mingled with Manhattan socialites and some of the United States' most prominent media figures.
They included Ted Turner, the founder of Cable News Network and now Time Warner vice chairman, and his wife, actress Jane Fonda.

Also attending were opera singer Beverly Sills; Sumner Redstone, the chairman and chief executive of Viacom Inc; and Steven Brill, the founder of the American Lawyer media group and the Court TV network.
Levin was to be buried at Sharon Gardens cemetery in Valhalla, New York.
